title: promotion-receipt/v0 independence policy
description: DRAFT (promotion-receipt/v0 draft_revision 2). Frozen policy fixture: an explicit set of `(effective_risk, predicate_id) -> acceptable {code, attestation}` tuples. NO numeric ordering exists anywhere in it -- evaluation is exact-key lookup on (effective_risk, predicate_id) plus set membership on (code, attestation); there is no risk fallback, no comparison between risks, no inheritance, and no first-match. The semantic MUSTs this schema cannot express (rule-key uniqueness, the rule-key manifest, code_classes disjointness and per-array uniqueness, acceptable tuple uniqueness, acceptable codes being technical-class only) are enforced by checkPolicy() in ../evaluate.mjs. `acceptable[].attestation` never admits `unknown` -- an unknown attestation can never satisfy a rule. A principal-class code may be REGISTERED in code_classes.principal (reserved for a future revision that has an authenticable principal source) but may never appear in acceptable[] in draft_revision 2 (it could never be satisfied -- see docs/protocols/promotion-receipt-v0.md). The receipt binds the JCS sha256 of this whole document as `independence_policy_digest`.

technical.description: Codes whose independence claim is about technical execution separation (provider / model family / session). A session ledger can at most attest these.

principal.description: Codes whose independence claim is about a human or organizational principal. Always evaluated to check=unknown in draft_revision 2 (no authenticable reviewer-principal source exists; approver authentication is not reviewer-independence authentication).
